To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
viral delivery of short interfering RNAs to mouse brain is an effective way to study the function of genes in drug addiction.
we have developed an approach to study the function of genes in mouse brain by stereotaxic injection of lentivirus expressing small-hairpins specific to the gene of interest.
lentiviral delivery of small-hairpin RNA to specific brain regions can be used to elucidate gene function in mouse models of drug addiction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of genes implicated in drug addiction using mouse behavioral models.
the neural mechanisms of drug addiction.
the functional neurobiology of drugs of abuse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protocol described here is a method for the stereotaxic injection of lentivirus to a precise location in mouse brain.

this method allows the researcher to determine the function of a gene of interest within a specific region of the mouse brain, by using lentiviral-mediated RNA interference to achieve sustained and specific knockdown of the target gene, and subsequently measuring the effects on behavior.

this protocol describes the stereotaxic surgery involved in the use of a lentiviral expression vector for RNA interference, in freely-moving adult mice, to knock down the endogenous expression of genes inside specific brain regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lentiviral vector system allows for long-term, gene-specific knockdown in vivo, in a site- and/or cell type-specific manner.
the lentiviral vector is a useful tool to knockdown gene expression and that it can be used to probe the function of specific genes in mouse brain.
we have demonstrated the use of RNA interference to knock down gene expression in the mouse brain and to study gene function with respect to behavioral phenotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
viral delivery of small-hairpin RNA to mouse brain is an effective method for studying the function of specific genes in behavioral models of addiction.
lentivirus can be used to deliver RNAi to a specific region of mouse brain, resulting in long-term knockdown of a specific gene.
lentivirus-mediated RNA interference can be used to study gene function in vivo in adult mice.
